models.title: Tax-drag proportion of potential gains
models.summary: Share of pretax gains consumed by taxes as the after-tax shortfall over the pretax gain.

relationship.original_equation: Tax drag = (Pretax future value − After-tax future value)/(Pretax future value − Initial investment)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Kozlowska cases, printed pp. 257–260 (PDF pp. 267–270): 89,611/286,968 = 31% (accrual) and 57,392/286,968 = 20% (deferred)
relationship.translation_notes: Inputs are accumulations/FVs (outputs of the FVIF siblings scaled by principal); td exceeds the nominal rate under accrual compounding and equals the rate under pure deferral (per source). Decimal form. Dimensional check: currency / currency = dimensionless share.

variables.definition: Pretax future accumulation, in currency units
variables.context: same investment, horizon and return as fvat

variables.definition: After-tax future accumulation, in currency units
variables.context: same investment, horizon and return as fvpt
variables.domain: At least p and at most fvpt

variables.definition: Initial amount invested, in the same currency units

variables.source_symbol: proportion of potential investment gains consumed by taxes
variables.definition: Proportion of potential pretax gains consumed by taxes, in decimal form
variables.context: same investment, horizon and return as inputs
variables.domain: Closed interval 0 to 1 under non-adverse taxation

assumptions: Same gross return path with and without taxes; the comparison isolates the tax effect (per source case studies).
limitations: Ex post attribution, not a forward rate: the share depends on horizon and return (per source Exhibit 25).
Adverse cases (after-tax below principal) fall outside the guarded domain.

models.title: Mortality-weighted human capital present value
models.summary: Human capital as survival-weighted discounted lifetime labor income.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM4 Life-Cycle View, printed p. 235 (PDF p. 245), Equation 1; Taylor case HC EUR636,156 at age 25
relationship.translation_notes: Family H holds the precomputed per-year summands h_t = p(st)·w_{t−1}(1+g_t)/(1+r_f+y)^t (currency present values; no elementwise family arithmetic in the grammar, so elements bind as computed values). Mortality weighting p(st), wage growth g_t and occupational-risk-adjusted discount r_f+y documented here. Dimensional check: sum of currency values.

variables.definition: Each year's survival-probability-weighted labor income discounted at the occupational-risk-adjusted rate, in currency units
variables.context: same individual, mortality table, wage path and discount rate; one element per working year

variables.definition: Human capital: mortality-weighted net present value of future labor income, in currency units
variables.context: same individual, mortality table, wage path and discount rate as H

assumptions: Actuarial survival probabilities from mortality tables; wage growth and occupational-risk premium y fixed over the horizon (per source).
Working life of N years; post-retirement pension values are separate (per source discussion).
limitations: Inputs are hard to estimate in practice (per source); the record formalizes the model, not the calibration.
Family size capped at 60 elements; longer horizons must be pre-aggregated.
Reference checks exercise aggregation of precomputed summands; the full 40-year Taylor evaluation (EUR636,156) is cited as evidence, not replayed element-by-element.

models.title: Domestic-currency return from foreign return and FX move
models.summary: Home-currency return as the product of foreign-asset and currency gross returns minus one.

relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Views of Currency Value Changes, printed p. 68 (PDF p. 78); portfolio form RDC = Σ ω_i(1 + R_FC,i)(1 + R_FX,i) − 1
relationship.translation_notes: Single-asset form recorded (the portfolio form is the weight-weighted sum of the same per-asset construction). Decimal form. Falls back to PDF-only provenance: no independent accessible corroboration found after textbook/curriculum-note searches. Dimensional check: dimensionless product minus one.

variables.definition: Return on the foreign-currency asset in its own currency, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset and period as rfx

variables.definition: Percentage change of the domestic currency versus the foreign currency (positive when the foreign currency strengthens), in decimal form
variables.context: same asset and period as rfc

variables.definition: Return in domestic (functional) currency terms, in decimal form
variables.context: same asset and period as inputs

assumptions: Single period; no hedging overlay (hedged proceeds follow interest parity, not this record).
limitations: First-order approximation RDC ≈ RFC + RFX drops the cross term; this record keeps it.
Portfolio form needs position weights summing to 1 (stated but not separately recorded).
unresolved: No accessible corroboration found after reasonable searches (textbook treatments state the economics without the formula; accessible hits were same-curriculum copies); formula verified only against the owner PDF, which reviewers cannot open.
